quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What can you do from the center lane?

options.text: Make left turns.
Make U-turns.
Pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: The center lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
See directly behind your vehicle.
See in your rearview mirror.
See in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers wear seat belts.
Make sure only adults wear seat belts.
Make sure only children wear seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car wears a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car wears a seat belt.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: ____ limit your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. You cannot drink and drive safely.

questions.question: Teen drivers are more likely to crash when:

options.text: Driving with a pet.
Driving with adult passengers.
Driving with teen passengers.
Driving alone.

questions.explanation: Teen drivers crash more often when other teens are in the car than when they drive alone or with adults.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Do nothing special.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you do not scare it.

questions.question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing signals or a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Listen for train sounds and watch for other warning signs.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less your tires grip the road. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on water.

questions.question: At a light rail crossing, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers need to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead shows red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead shows green.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal at the next intersection.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists don't have to obey traffic laws.
They can be ticketed.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop your vehicle unless you are already inside the intersection.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If someone is following too close, slow down gradually and let them pass. Following too closely causes most rear-end crashes.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Don't speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires properly filled with air.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase this risk.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
Stay in the right lane only.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without hard braking. This prevents crashes with cars behind you.

questions.question: What following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle?

options.text: At least two car lengths.
At least two seconds.
At least four seconds.
At least four motorcycle lengths.

questions.explanation: On dry roads, four seconds of space is a safe following distance. Keep extra space behind motorcycles.
